core_obligations: Reduce to the case of sets (proof lines 2879-2889): if the category is cofibred in sets the statement follows from the Schlessinger description of (S2) together with the identification of k[V] with a product of copies of k[epsilon] indexed by a basis of V.

Induct on the dimension and produce the object (proof lines 2889-2996): write V = V' direct sum k epsilon; given a diagram over A and k[V], choose morphisms to the objects over k[V'] and k[epsilon], apply the induction hypothesis to get y' over A x_k k[V'], and then apply (S2) for the extension k[epsilon] to obtain y over (A x_k k[V']) x_k k[epsilon], which is A x_k k[V]; pushing y forward to y_V over k[V] and comparing with x_V through the second half of (S2) produces the isomorphism making y fit into the required diagram, so the existence half holds.

Prove the injectivity half (proof lines 2998-3092): given two diagrams as in the second half of (S2) with k[V], push both objects to A x_k k[V'] and use the induction hypothesis together with the axioms of cofibred categories to obtain compatible morphisms to x_{V'}; the resulting two commutative diagrams over A x_k k[epsilon] admit an isomorphism by the second half of (S2) for k[epsilon], and the resulting isomorphism between the two objects is compatible with the maps to the fibre product and hence with the maps to x, which is exactly the required injectivity.
proof_roadmap: Dispose of the case of the associated category in sets by the Schlessinger description of (S2).
Implement the induction on the dimension for the existence half by splitting off one coordinate and applying (S2) for the trivial extension.
Prove the injectivity half by the same splitting, using the induction hypothesis and (S2) for the trivial extension.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a category cofibred in groupoids satisfying (S2) satisfies the same condition with the algebra of dual numbers replaced by the algebra of a finite dimensional vector space (statement lines 2871-2877). The proof (proof lines 2879-3092) handles the case of sets through the Schlessinger description and then runs an induction on the dimension splitting off one coordinate, proving the existence and the injectivity halves of the condition by comparing objects through the two halves of (S2). H3: a full induction with a genuine splitting argument on both halves of the condition, written out in full.
